title: Comparison with completed coefficients
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $X$ be a scheme, and let $E\subseteq\Qlb$ be a finite extension
of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\cO_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$. For a condensed
ring $\Lambda$ write $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ for its pullback to $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$
along $p_X\colon\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}})\to\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}})$
([sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]). Write
$\cO_{E,X}$, $E_X$ and $\QbarX$ for the pullbacks to $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ of the condensed
rings $\underline{\cO_E}$, $\underline E$ ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]) and
$\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]). There are canonical isomorphisms of
sheaves of rings

$$
\cO_{E,X}\cong\varprojlim_n(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X,
\qquad E_X\cong\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell],
\qquad \QbarX\cong\varinjlim_E E_X,
$$

where $(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ is the constant sheaf, $\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell]$ is the colimit in sheaves of $\cO_{E,X}$-modules of
$\cO_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ell}\cO_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots$, equipped with its
localization ring structure, and the last colimit runs
over the filtered poset of finite subextensions $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Qlb$,
with transition maps induced by the inclusions $\underline E\to\underline F\to\underline{\Qlb}$.
They are compatible with inverse image along every morphism of schemes.

For $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ this gives
$\mathbf Z_{\ell,X}\simeq\varprojlim_n(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_X$ and
$\mathbf Q_{\ell,X}\simeq\mathbf Z_{\ell,X}[1/\ell]$.

proof.text: Use the integral-limit detail module’s underlying-set pullback comparison and representable pullback construction. For the specified powers of the uniformizer, compactness of the integer ring and surjectivity of reduction give a compatible preimage by nested closed fibres; adic separatedness gives uniqueness. The relative profinite test functor preserves this tower limit, and Yoneda transports it to the underlying sheaves. The ring-object limit property follows by checking unit and multiplication against the jointly distinguishing projections. The finite discrete point comparison and the constant-sheaf pullback comparison identify every level with its constant ring, naturally in the actual quotient transitions.

The inversion lemma identifies the module telescope with $E_X$ as a sheaf of rings, using exactly the legs $\ell^{-m}\varphi$ of the integral inclusion. Invert its canonical isomorphism to obtain the second comparison.

Apply [lem-sfb-qlbar-point-abelian-colimit] to the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring. The actual inclusions $j_E$ give a colimit in condensed abelian groups. The index contains $\mathbf Q_\ell$, is directed by composita, and is a small set of subfields of the fixed $\Qlb$.

source.place: Third isomorphism: explicit point-colimit universal property

proof.text: The left adjoint $p_X^*$ preserves the colimit in step 3; its image is exactly the cocone of [def-sfb-qlbar-x-cocone], a colimit in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$. Its terms, vertex and legs are ring objects and ring-object morphisms, since [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] makes $\Lambda\mapsto\Lambda_X$ a functor on ring objects. The index poset is filtered: it contains $\mathbf Q_\ell$, is directed by [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and has at most one arrow between two objects. By the sheaf-tensor theorem each functor $Y\otimes-$ and $-\otimes Y$ has a right adjoint and so preserves colimits. Hence [lem-sfb-filtered-ring-object-cocone-colimit] applies: the cocone is a colimit in ring objects, and also in commutative ring objects since $\QbarX$ and all $E_X$ are commutative.

source.place: Third isomorphism: transport the abelian cocone and lift its ring structure

proof.text: Apply clauses (1), (2), (3) of the pullback-comparison lemma to any scheme map $f:X\to Y$. They give compatibility of the three canonical comparisons, including preservation of this particular integral limit and every colimit leg.

Apply the same represented compact-tower construction directly to the usual maps PadicInt.toZModPow with values ZMod (ell^(n+1)). Their standard compatibility, surjectivity and joint injectivity give the normalized integral limit. The finite constant comparisons are natural in the cast homomorphisms. Transport the normalized cones along the monoidal coefficient pullback compositor to obtain preservation by every scheme inverse image; naturality of the reductions is the compositor naturality equation. The rational specialization uses the existing continuous-integral telescope for Q_ell.

source.place: Final Q_ell specialization in the statement

No new holed results.

lean.statement: theorem completedCondensedIntegral (X : Scheme.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l) (π : PadicAlgCl.integers l E) (hπ : Ideal.span {π} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (PadicAlgCl.integers l E)) : (∃ (c : Cone (Functor.ofOpSequence (X := fun n ↦ completedCoefficient X (Profinite.continuousMapRingSheaf (completedResidue l E π n))) (fun n ↦ completedCoefficientMap X (completedResidueTransition l E π n)))) (e : completedCoefficient X (Profinite.padicIntegersCondensedRing l E) ≅ c.pt), (∀ n, e.hom ≫ c.π.app (op n) = completedCoefficientMap X (completedReduction l E π n)) ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit c)) ∧ (∀ n, Finite (completedResidue l E π n)) ∧ (∃ k : ∀ n, completedCoefficient X (Profinite.continuousMapRingSheaf (completedResidue l E π n)) ≅ completedConstantRing X (completedResidue l E π n), ∀ n, completedCoefficientMap X (completedResidueTransition l E π n) ≫ (k n).hom = (k (n + 1)).hom ≫ completedConstantMap X (Ideal.Quotient.factorPow (Ideal.span {π}) (Nat.le_succ (n + 1))))
lean.note: The six theorem declarations jointly state all three comparisons, arbitrary inverse-image compatibility, and the explicit Z_l/Q_l specializations. Integral comparisons use normalized IsLimit cones in ring objects; rational comparisons use the canonical module-colimit universal property on the existing rational ring; the finite-field ring cocone is an IsColimit. Helper definitions only bundle existing coefficient objects and their actual maps.
